reasons: X has the most rigorous structure. The budget sums exactly to Rs 10,00,000, and I re-checked the ladder arithmetic (59 step-days at Rs 3,000 gives Rs 1,77,000). Its kill and scale rules are tied to a stated break-even cost per purchase. It also checks the learning-phase maths and says honestly that the test ad sets screen ideas rather than prove them. Z is nearly as sound and the cleanest to read. It keeps spend in one sales campaign, gives dated order-by cut-offs, and does not promise a forecast. Its Gehna specifics are strong. Y spreads the money across six campaigns, which starves each of purchase data. Its targets contradict each other, and it publishes a revenue forecast with no basis in Gehna data. All three flagged the Mumbai versus Chennai mismatch correctly. X leaks internal file references and a persona the client cannot see, so it would need light editing before sending.

biggest_flaw.X: Refers to internal files and a persona the client cannot see, and the dense tables make it heavier to read.
biggest_flaw.Y: Too many campaigns for the budget, and a made-up revenue forecast with inconsistent CPA and ROAS targets.
biggest_flaw.Z: Test lane and WhatsApp assumptions (1 in 10 chats become orders) are working estimates, and the scale rules are less formal than X's.

best_thing.X: Exact budget and ladder maths, a clear break-even cost per purchase, and test rules a media buyer could follow from day one.
best_thing.Y: Detailed copy and a production list, plus useful ideas on WhatsApp offline-event tracking and on risks.
best_thing.Z: Dated order-by cut-offs tied to wedding dates and Gehna's own delivery times, with real named pieces and prices in every ad.
